chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v01] The path of art will be spoken according to glorious Shambhava knowledge.

[tal-a11-v10] It is united in all directions in the abode of the expansion of freedom; but from freedom its own form does not fall away from the nature of the knower.

[tal-a11-v02] As in the previously stated middle of the world, after each group follows its own, a separate principle is said to be called.

[tal-a11-v03] Thus, among those principles too, that which is of the nature of approach to its own class and separated from the other class is called kala in the teaching of Shiva.

[tal-a11-v04] Some say that this power, again, is the very subtle power within the principles; it is called kalā, as the bearer in earth.

[tal-a11-v05] Here the thing does not appear divided in two alternatives, because a universal is not accepted as following, unlike the Nyāyikas and others.

[tal-a11-v06] Others say that at the beginning of initiation, for the purpose of easy collection, Shiva devised a class called kala, which is samaya-dependent.

[tal-a11-v07] The covenant made by the God of gods does not reach ultimate reality; yet it is not false, and no other covenant arises.

[tal-a11-v08] Cessation belongs to the earth-principle, establishment to the manifest perceptible domain, knowledge to the end of night, and peace to the end of power; this egg is four.

[tal-a11-v09] In the Shiva-principle beyond peace, supreme Shiva is beyond kala; here there is no classification, convention, or even counting.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-:C11 atha śrītantrāloke ekādaśamāhnikam kalādhvā vakṣyate śrīmacchāṃbhavājñānusārataḥ yathā pūrvoktabhuvanamadhye nijanijaṃ gaṇam / anuyatparato bhinnaṃ tattvaṃ nāmeti bhaṇyate tathā teṣvapi tattveṣu svavarge@nugamātmakam / vyāvṛttaṃ paravargācca kaleti śivaśāsane kecidāhuḥ punaryāsau śaktirantaḥ susūkṣmikā / tattvānāṃ sā kaletyuktā dharaṇyāṃ dhārikā yathā atra pakṣadvaye vastu na bhinnaṃ bhāsate yataḥ / anugāmi na sāmānyamiṣṭaṃ naiyāyikādivat anye vadanti dīkṣādau sukhasaṃgrahaṇārthataḥ / śivena kalpito vargaḥ kaleti samayāśrayaḥ kṛtaśca devadevena samayo@paramārthatām / na gacchatīti nāsatyo na cānyasamayodayaḥ nivṛttiḥ pṛthivītattve pratiṣṭhāvyaktagocare / vidyā niśānte śāntā ca śaktyante@ṇḍamidaṃ catuḥ śāntātītā śive tattve kalātītaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ / nahyatra vargīkaraṇaṃ samayaḥ kalanāpi vā yujyate sarvatodikkaṃ svātantryollāsadhāmani / svātantryāttu nijaṃ rūpaṃ boddhṛdharmādavicyutam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v11] For the establishment of ultimate reality through instruction and immersion in that, the god who brings understanding is clearly manifested.

[tal-a11-v12] Because even in the Shiva principle a union of kalās is declared; and the cosmic egg is named the cause of the establishment of world-divisions.

[tal-a11-v13] They call 'covering' that which ends in power, as long as it exists; although before, even in the principle called Śiva, there is the world-path.

[tal-a11-v14] It has been said; yet even in the unobstructed, there is no occurrence of veiling in this. But thus, having left earth, [one is] in the powers of prakṛti and māyā.

[tal-a11-v15] Even in non-obstruction, how does the egg originate? Here our teachers say it is the five beginning with earth.

[tal-a11-v16] This appears directly, and nothing else exists; in measurability, gross and subtle distinctions arise through instrumentality.

[tal-a11-v17] From the exultation of the agent, in the state of agency, the thirty principles are clearly set forth as having the nature of difference; their non-difference is considered night.

[tal-a11-v18] When distinctions such as effectness and instrumentness dissolve, in the state of supreme independent expansion, they sang the fivefold ending in Shiva.

[tal-a11-v19] It is declared abundantly in the glorious Kalottara and other texts; thus these five principles indeed pervade the whole world.

[tal-a11-v20] In the five-mantra body, sadyojata and the rest are said up to Ishana; there, from earth to the end of sky.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-upadeśatadāveśaparamārthatvasiddhaye / bodhyatāmānayandevaḥ sphuṭameva vibhāvyate yato@taḥ śivatattve@pi kalāsaṃgatirucyate / aṇḍaṃ ca nāma bhuvanavibhāgasthitikāraṇam prāhurāvaraṇaṃ tacca śaktyantaṃ yāvadasti hi / yadyapi prāk śivākhye@pi tattve bhuvanapaddhatiḥ uktā tathāpyapratighe nāsminnāvṛtisaṃbhavaḥ / nanvevaṃ dharaṇīṃ muktvā śaktau prakṛtimāyayoḥ api cāpratighatve@pi kathamaṇḍasya saṃbhavaḥ / atrāsmadguravaḥ prāhuryatpṛthivyādipañcakam pratyakṣamidamābhāti tato@nyannāsti kiṃcana / meyatve sthūlasūkṣmatvānmānatve karaṇatvataḥ kartṛtollāsataḥ kartṛbhāve sphuṭatayoditam / triṃśattattvaṃ vibhedātma tadabhedo niśā matā kāryatvakaraṇatvādivibhāgagalane sati / vikāsotkasvatantratve śivāntaṃ pañcakaṃ jaguḥ śrīmatkālottarādau ca kathitaṃ bhūyasā tathā / pañcaitāni tu tattvāni yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat pañcamantratanau tena sadyojātādi bhaṇyate / īśānāntaṃ tatra tatra dharādigaganāntakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v21] From the Shiva principle comes the void beyond void, which would be unattached; but the Shiva principle itself is the self of all non-difference, independent, and beautiful consciousness.

[tal-a11-v22] But the thirty-seventh they call the principle named Para-Shiva; even that, by the stated method, is imagined in the knowable state there.

[tal-a11-v23] When it abides unbounded, that is called the thirty-eighth; there is no regress, and thus it would be seen by great souls.

[tal-a11-v24] What is knowable shines; when it disappears, what shines forth is tattva; thus the thirty-six shine in the heart.

[tal-a11-v25] Then what? Not something or? The body, in dependence on desire for something, is consciousness-bliss-independent one-form? That, thus, in teaching.

[tal-a11-v26] The thirty-seventh shines equally; there is no other expectation there; and that too is an established knowability where it shines; that is made of consciousness.

[tal-a11-v27] He too is taught by meditation as the thirty-eighth; if indeed, then the thirty-seventh would become again.

[tal-a11-v28] The nature of non-difference, independence, consciousness-fullness, and the like is indeed the same; making something known is only more than that, because...

[tal-a11-v29] On earth, at the end of the guna-tattva and at the end of maya, they are situated gradually: smell, taste, and form within, by the sequence of subtle beings, but...

[tal-a11-v30] Thus, with the doctrine established, even at the end of the śakti-tattva there is some subtle touch, which yogis always desire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śivatattvamataḥ śūnyātiśūnyaṃ syādanāśri[vṛ]tam / yattu sarvāvibhāgātma svatantraṃ bodhasundaram saptatriṃśaṃ tu tatprāhustattvaṃ paraśivābhidham / tasyāpyuktanayādvedyabhāve@tra parikalpite yadāste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadaṣṭātriṃśamucyate / na cānavasthā hyevaṃ syāddṛśyatāṃ hi mahātmabhiḥ yadvedyaṃ kiṃcidābhāti tatkṣaye yatprakāśate / tattattvamiti nirṇītaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ hṛdi bhāsate tatkiṃ na kiṃcidvā kiṃcidityākāṅkṣāvaśe vapuḥ / cidānandasvatantraikarūpaṃ taditi deśane saptatriṃśaṃ samābhāti tatrākāṅkṣā ca nāparā / taccāpi klṛptavedyatvaṃ yatra bhāti sa cinmayaḥ aṣṭātriṃśattamaḥ so@pi bhāvanāyopadiśyate / yadi nāma tataḥ saptatriṃśa eva punarbhavet avibhāgasvatantratvacinmayatvādidharmatā / samaiva vedyīkaraṇaṃ kevalaṃ tvadhikaṃ yataḥ dharāyāṃ guṇatattvānte māyānte kramaśaḥ sthitāḥ / gandho raso rūpamantaḥ sūkṣmabhāvakrameṇa tu iti sthite naye śaktitattvānte@pyasti saukṣmyabhāk / sparśaḥ ko@pi sadā yasmai yoginaḥ spṛhayālavaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v31] But at the end of that touch, awareness, shaped as pure consciousness-space, in which one is established, approaches the supreme self-luminous.

[tal-a11-v32] Therefore from the bindu comes sound; from that comes form; from that comes taste; thus is said of agitation-nature in spanda; but touch is not so.

[tal-a11-v33] The opinion of Caitanya-Maheśa, which Śrī formerly spoke, is a nourishing sustainer, enlightener, purifier, and giver of space.

[tal-a11-v34] By these words dealing with nivṛtti and the rest, one's own body is the five-element rule that has been stated; now the three principles are described.

[tal-a11-v35] The self reaches only up to vijnanakala; beyond that, in the remainder ending in vidyesvara, Shiva may be in three principles or in one principle, and Shiva is supreme.

[tal-a11-v36] These two differences are produced solely by tattva-difference; thus, in the tattva-adhvan there is loss, but there is no loss from the establishment of the six adhvans.

[tal-a11-v37] Nature, puruṣa, time, māyā, vidyeśa, sauśiva, and Śiva are principles; even in the nine-principle rule, there is the form of the essence-sacrifice.

[tal-a11-v38] Thus, in the procedure called eighteen, the wise would state the law: wherever there is desire for enjoyment, it is applied according to its predominance and usefulness.

[tal-a11-v39] And from other inner contemplation, initiation has endless distinctions; by that, from thirty-six until the rite of the single principle becomes.

[tal-a11-v40] This truth-path was indeed spoken by God, in detail and in brief; this one truth-rule is for the well-awakened guru.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tatsparśānte tu saṃvittiḥ śuddhacidvyomarūpiṇī / yasyāṃ rūḍhaḥ samabhyeti svaprakāśātmikāṃ parām ato vindurato nādo rūpamasmādato rasaḥ / ityuktaṃ kṣobhakatvena spande sparśastu no tathā mataṃ caitanmaheśasya śrīpūrve yadabhāṣata / dhārikāpyāyinī boddhrī pavitrī cāvakāśadā ebhiḥ śabdairvyavaharan nivṛttyādernijaṃ vapuḥ / pañcatattvavidhiḥ proktastritattvamadhunocyate vijñānākalaparyantamātmā vidyeśvarāntakam / śeṣe śivastritattve syādekatattve śivaḥ param imau bhedāvubhau tattvabhedamātrakṛtāviti / tattvādhvaivāyamitthaṃ ca na ṣaḍadhvasthiteḥ kṣatiḥ prakṛt pumānyatiḥ kālo māyā vidyeśasauśivau / śivaśca navatattve@pi vidhau tattvādhvarūpatā evamaṣṭādaśākhye@pi vidhau nyāyaṃ vadetsudhīḥ / yatra yatra hi bhogecchā tatprādhānyopayogataḥ anyāntarbhāvanātaśca dīkṣānantavibhedabhāk / tena ṣaṭtriṃśato yāvadekatattvavidhirbhavet tattvādhvaiva sa devena prokto vyāsasamāsataḥ / ekatattvavidhiścaiṣa suprabuddhaṃ guruṃ prati

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v41] The disciple is delighted by Shambhu because the hope of enjoyment has departed; difference is expanded by Shambhu's self-willed power.

[tal-a11-v42] The Lord always rests in the non-different self; thus the threefold path differs as gross, subtle, and supreme.

[tal-a11-v43] The one who has entered the measurable part is called the city-principle-phase self; now the form situated in the maternal part is determined in three ways.

[tal-a11-v44] The measure-natured form of the path that reaches the mother-part is called a word, because comprehension merges into self-nature.

[tal-a11-v45] That indeed is the word, the mantra, fallen from agitation, when the secret-speaker becomes silent and established, because the mother.

[tal-a11-v46] Nevertheless, he does not abandon the form of the self of reflection; by that he is the self of measure and reflection, not like a man subject to agitation.

[tal-a11-v47] In the Trika teaching, the mantras and words spoken by him have an own form that is indeed undivided, supreme in agitated non-vibration.

[tal-a11-v48] When indifference is abandoned and agitation descends, the path of phonemes comes into play; in the Mother-portion that valid cognition would be the one stated before.

[tal-a11-v49] She is, however, non-different because of her full essence; therefore, in truth, each letter is one, beginning from patience.

[tal-a11-v50] Having done [the rite] in supreme Śaiva, the sixteen-syllabled [mantra] is declared from visarga; there, so much śakti-vibration is determined beforehand.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śiṣyaṃ ca gatabhogāśamuditaḥ śaṃbhunā yataḥ / bhedaṃ visphārya visphārya śaktyā svacchandarūpayā svātmanyabhinne bhagavānnityaṃ viśramayan sthitaḥ / itthaṃ tryātmādhvano bhedaḥ sthūlasūkṣmaparatvataḥ meyabhāgagataḥ proktaḥ puratattvakalātmakaḥ / adhunā mātṛbhāgasthaṃ rūpaṃ tredhā nirūpyate yatpramāṇātmakaṃ rūpamadhvano mātṛbhāgagam / padaṃ hyavagamātmatvasamāveśāttaducyate tadeva ca padaṃ mantraḥ prakṣobhātpracyutaṃ yadā / guptabhāṣī yato mātā tūṣṇīṃbhūto vyavasthitaḥ tathāpi na vimarśātma rūpaṃ tyajati tena saḥ / pramāṇātmavimarśātmā mānavatkṣobhabhāṅnatu mantrāṇāṃ ca padānāṃ ca tenoktaṃ trikaśāsane / abhinnameva svaṃ rūpaṃ niḥspandakṣobhite param audāsīnyaparityāge prakṣobhānavarohaṇe / varṇādhvā mātṛbhāge syāt pūrvaṃ yā kathitā pramā sā tu pūrṇasvarūpatvādavibhāgamayī yataḥ / tata ekaikavarṇatvaṃ tattve tattve kṣamāditaḥ kṛtvā śaive pare proktāḥ ṣoḍaśārṇā visargataḥ / tatra śaktiparispandastāvān prāk ca nirūpitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v51] Now everything is summed up: in bliss-consciousness one holds a single sixteen-fold mantra syllable or word; and cessation is another mantra word—truth-syllable, fire-eye, city-arrow-essence.

[tal-a11-v52] The sage-principle syllable is a two-foot mantra; the fire-syllable principle is a one-foot mantra; and the army-world is thus the fourth.

[tal-a11-v53] Sixteen letters and one pada-mantra principle, beyond peace, were spoken by Abhinavagupta to the three noble ones for the disciples' summary.

[tal-a11-v54] That entire path, possessing the mode of non-difference from Bhairava, shines by attaining autonomy from its freedom.

[tal-a11-v55] For thus, abiding in mother-form, the mantra-path is determined; for thus, when the expressible state is swallowed by consciousness-reflection.

[tal-a11-v56] Intent on protecting meditation dependent on Shiva's knowledge and action, from skill and eagerness in the play of unlimited multitudes of powers.

[tal-a11-v57] Fallen from measure-made form and gone into the consciousness-mantra paths, having attained measure-form, the path goes to the state of word-self.

[tal-a11-v58] Thus indeed, the mother's rest assembles many letters; collision and sequential process are speech-nature indeed, that.

[tal-a11-v59] Imagination's own form is clearly made of enjoyment-entrancement; therefore our teacher sang it as the form of validity.

[tal-a11-v60] Without abandoning entry into the form of pramana, measurability...
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saṃkalayyocyate sarvamadhunā sukhasaṃvide / padamantravarṇamekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ / tattvārṇamagninayanaṃ rasaśarapuramastramantrapadamanyā munitattvārṇaṃ dvikapadamantraṃ vasvakṣibhuvanamaparakalā / agnyarṇatattvamekakapadamantraṃ sainyabhuvanamiti turyā ṣoḍaśa varṇāḥ padamantratattvamekaṃ ca śāntyatīteyam / abhinavaguptenāryātrayamuktaṃ saṃgrahāya śiṣyebhyaḥ so@yaṃ samasta evādhvā bhairavābhedavṛttimān / tatsvātantryātsvatantratvamaśnuvāno@vabhāsate tathāhi mātṛrūpastho mantrādhveti nirūpitaḥ / tathāhi cidvimarśena grastā vācyadaśā yadā śivajñānakriyāyattamananatrāṇatatparā / aśeṣaśaktipaṭalīlīlālāmpaṭyapāṭavāt cyutā mānamayādrūpāt saṃvinmantrādhvatāṃ gatā / pramāṇarūpatāmetya prayātyadhvā padātmatām tathā hi māturviśrāntirvarṇānsaṃghaṭya tānbahūn / saṃghaṭṭanaṃ ca kramikaṃ saṃjalpātmakameva tat vikalpasya svakaṃ rūpaṃ bhogāveśamayaṃ sphuṭam / ataḥ pramāṇatārūpaṃ padamasmadgururjagau pramāṇarūpatāveśamaparityajya meyatām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v61] The path that proceeds by calculation from yoga is declared to consist of parts; in pure union of measurability it has a share of subtle and gross.

[tal-a11-v62] In the state of the reality-path and world-path, the guru follows in order the form situated above of the measurable, the means, and the knowers.

[tal-a11-v63] Let the sound-self indeed be seen by yogins who taste rest in rising consciousness, abiding in meditation on the supreme self only.

[tal-a11-v64] From the power of all designations, unrestrained powers are created; in the meaning that arises together with the self, they extend as far as earth.

[tal-a11-v65] Considering in the ground of consciousness, those streams of letters bear consciousness as true valid cognition, without distinction among so many objects.

[tal-a11-v66] Children and animals are also cognizers; even those who share no convention have, through innate refinement, this very self-awareness.

[tal-a11-v67] Having resorted to various distinct things, they attain variegated cognizer-hood; rootedness is in this natural, infinite consciousness of varṇas.

[tal-a11-v68] Conventions pass away; even if they enter an unsymbolic state. But without this, all conventions are made again and again.

[tal-a11-v69] By unceasingness they would make an insurmountable regress; a child is instructed there by that, through seeking convention.

[tal-a11-v70] Even when this is pointed out with a finger, the mind is not nonconceptual; conceptualization is rooted in word, and word lives by convention.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-gacchankalanayā yogādadhvā proktaḥ kalātmakaḥ / śuddhe prameyatāyoge sūkṣmasthūlatvabhāgini tattvādhvabhuvanādhvatve krameṇānusaredguruḥ / prameyamānamātṝṇāṃ yadrūpamupari sthitam pramātmātra sthito@dhvāyaṃ varṇātmā dṛśyatāṃ kila / ucchalatsaṃvidāmātraviśrāntyāsvādayoginaḥ sarvābhidhānasāmarthyādaniyantritaśaktayaḥ / sṛṣṭāḥ svātmasahotthe@rthe dharāparyantabhāgini āmṛśantaḥ svacidbhūmau tāvato@rthānabhedataḥ / varṇaughāste pramārūpāṃ satyāṃ bibhrati saṃvidam bālāstiryakpramātāro ye@pyasaṃketabhāginaḥ / te@pyakṛtrimasaṃskārasārāmenāṃ svasaṃvidam bhinnabhinnāmupāśritya yānti citrāṃ pramātṛtām / asyā cākṛtrimānantavarṇasaṃvidi rūḍhatām saṃketā yānti cette@pi yāntyasaṃketavṛttitām / anayā tu vinā sarve saṃketā bahuśaḥ kṛtāḥ aviśrāntatayā kuryuranavasthāṃ duruttarām / bālo vyutpādyate yena tatra saṃketamārgaṇāt aṅgulyādeśane@pyasya nāvikalpā tathā matiḥ / vikalpaḥ śabdamūlaśca śabdaḥ saṃketajīvitaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v71] By that infinite, indeed illusion-free, he who is such a group of letters, companion of the reflection of consciousness, always indeed expands.

[tal-a11-v72] Since indeed the māyic colors spread birth, and those are determined as potency within the māyic colors.

[tal-a11-v73] They are indifferent to convention; let their proceeding be accepted, for when others' words are heard, one's own is covered.

[tal-a11-v74] Whose valid knowledge is dull does not approach there for that purpose; motherhood; the parrot-child indeed reads the supreme, a one-share-holder in that order.

[tal-a11-v75] But indeed, whose knowerhood is from the gain of independence? In the gain of self-statement pramā, self-pramā-awareness is from the exposure and refutation of opponents.

[tal-a11-v76] In the heap of letters beginning with a sentence, the knower becomes master in his own form, as the unmade form is distinguished from that form.

[tal-a11-v77] Thus wonder is perceived in gradation: immersed within the first mayic letter, and likewise in each subsequent one.

[tal-a11-v78] In Saketa, in the immersion of the previous-previous part, those distinct in splendor are established in the splendor-self, even in the greatness of initial excess.

[tal-a11-v79] Certainly, they attain an abundance of poetic speech from all sides as long as they remain in the abode where convention is abandoned.

[tal-a11-v80] One who rests in consciousness—what does he not know, what does he not do? Therefore, indeed, in the accomplishment of speech, the letters are to be worshipped.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tenānanto hyamāyīyo yo varṇagrāma īdṛśaḥ / saṃvidvimarśasacivaḥ sadaiva sa hi jṛmbhate yata eva ca māyīyā varṇāḥ sūtiṃ vitenire / ye ca māyīyavarṇeṣu vīryatvena nirūpitāḥ saṃketanirapekṣāste prameti parigṛhyatām / tathā hi paravākyeṣu śruteṣvāvriyate nijā pramā yasya jaḍo@sau no tatrārthe@bhyeti mātṛtām / śukavatsa paṭhatyeva paraṃ tatkramitaikabhāk svātantryalābhataḥ svākyapramālābhe tu boddhṛtā / yasya hi svapramābodho vipakṣodbhedanigrahāt vākyādivarṇapuñje sve sa pramātā vaśībhavet / yathā yathā cākṛtakaṃ tadrūpamatiricyate tathā tathā camatkāratāratamyaṃ vibhāvyate / ādyāmāyīyavarṇāntarnimagne cottarottare sakete pūrvapūrvāṃśamajjane pratibhābhidaḥ / ādyodrekamahattve@pi pratibhātmani niṣṭhitāḥ dhruvaṃ kavitvavaktṛtvaśālitāṃ yānti sarvataḥ / yāvaddhāmani saṃketanikārakalanojjhite viśrāntaścinmaye kiṃ kiṃ na vetti kurute na vā / ata eva hi vāksiddhau varṇānāṃ samupāsyatā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v81] Or, in the accomplishment of omniscience and the rest, what accomplishment is not made of that? This is stated by Varada in the doctrine of Śrī Siddhayogīśvarī.

[tal-a11-v82] By that hidden one, the remaining letters are protected; thus clearly, he who appears is characterized by I-ness, measurability, and knowability.

[tal-a11-v83] In the purification of one's own body, six-fold, he attains purification by the path; by the purification of one body, there indeed arises another kind.

[tal-a11-v84] The guru who internalizes, practices, and possesses purity and investigation...; but if the power of internalization is absent, he should purify subtly, subtly.

[tal-a11-v85] That which is purified, from its seed-nature, does not produce a later continuity; purification in many ways is the single continuity of attaining that enjoyment.

[tal-a11-v86] That sovereignty, that abandonment, that knowledge of Shiva-selfhood, that absorption, that rejection—all of this occurs by order and disorder.

[tal-a11-v87] Therefore those mantras, purifying and of varied forms, spread a variegated purification in the siddhanta, vama, daksha, and related streams.

[tal-a11-v88] The mantras of the sequence called the unsurpassed triad are indeed all all-giving; but primacy belongs to one of them somewhere.

[tal-a11-v89] Therefore, in the scripture called Śrīpūrva, the arrangement of the mantras beginning with parāpara is set forth in the mantra-path, in a purifying manner.

[tal-a11-v90] Purifying-ness applies to the impurity of the goddesses, the triad, the three deities, and the eight faces/limbs.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sarvajñatvādisiddhau vā kā siddhiryā na tanmayī / taduktaṃ varadena śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate tena guptena guptāste śeṣā varṇāstviti sphuṭam / evaṃ māmātṛmānatvameyatvairyo@vabhāsate ṣaḍvidhaḥ svavapuḥśuddhau śuddhiṃ so@dhvādhigacchati / ekena vapuṣā śuddhau tatraivānyaprakāratām antarbhāvyācarecchuddhimanusaṃdhānavān guruḥ / anantarbhāvaśaktau tu sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tu śodhayet tadviśuddhaṃ bījabhāvāt sūte nottarasaṃtatim / śodhanaṃ bahudhā tattadbhogaprāptyekatānatā tadādhipatyaṃ tattyāgastacchivātmatvavedanam / tallīnatā tannirāsaḥ sarvaṃ caitatkramākramāt ata eva ca te mantrāḥ śodhakāścitrarūpiṇaḥ / siddhāntavāmadakṣādau citrāṃ śuddhiṃ vitanvate anuttaratrikānāmakramamantrāstu ye kila / te sarve sarvadāḥ kintu kasyācit kvāpi mukhyatā ataḥ śodhakabhāvena śāstre śrīpūrvasaṃjñite / parāparādimantrāṇāmadhvanyuktā vyavasthitiḥ śodhakatvaṃ ca mālinyā devīnāṃ tritayasya ca / devatrayasya vaktrāṇāmaṅgānāmaṣṭakasya ca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v100] In the circle of beings, the differentiating non-reflection 'thus I am' is the Bhairava-full part, one-cin-matra.

[tal-a11-v91] What need of too much? In the order of door, site, support, and guru, in the rite of world-protector weapons, having omitted mantras, all is purifying.

[tal-a11-v92] And this purifiability of the path is declared, and that which is purified is said to be fit, from autonomy, in difference from Shiva, and in scripture.

[tal-a11-v93] All this indeed shines in the supreme, fixed Lord by reflection-form, not by externality, because [the reason is left implicit].

[tal-a11-v94] In Shiva there is only consciousness-space; the samsarins' thought of body and the like as distinct is like the thought of snake, rope, and wave.

[tal-a11-v95] Since the doctrine established before the body's death is within the range of dream, in death beginning with another body, what kind is the origin of the body?

[tal-a11-v96] Even in a dream, particulars appear through the force of the common manifestation of mere appearance; they are not even imagined as such.

[tal-a11-v97] Just as some salagrama stones bear variegated forms, so too are hearts painted with variegated lines at the end of the ground of maya and the rest.

[tal-a11-v98] Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like, following that will, are not self-existent; they are neither good nor bad, nor are they of the nature of cause or non-cause.

[tal-a11-v99] From the cutting off of long-established niyati and the arising of the unestablished, this independent Bhairava stands in the space of consciousness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-kiṃ vātibahunā dvāravāstvādhāragurukrame / lokapāstravidhau mantrān muktvā sarvaṃ viśodhakam yaccaitadadhvanaḥ proktaṃ śodhyatvaṃ śoddhṛtā ca yā / sā svātantryācchivābhede yuktetyuktaṃ ca śāsane sarvametadvibhātyeva parameśitari dhruve / pratibimbasvarūpeṇa na tu bāhyatayā yataḥ cidvyomnyeva śive tattaddehādimatirīdṛśī / bhinnā saṃsāriṇāṃ rajjau sarpasragvīcibuddhivat yataḥ prāgdehamaraṇasiddhāntaḥ svapnagocaraḥ / dehāntarādirmaraṇe kīdṛgvā dehasaṃbhavaḥ svapne@pi pratibhāmātrasāmānyaprathanābalāt / viśeṣāḥ pratibhāsante na bhāvyante@pi te yathā śālagrāmopalāḥ keciccitrākṛtibhṛto yathā / tathā māyādibhūmyantalekhācitrahṛdaścitaḥ nagarārṇavaśailādyāstadicchānuvidhāyinaḥ / na svayaṃ sadasanto no kāraṇākāraṇātmakāḥ niyateścirarūḍhāyāḥ samucchedātpravartanāt / arūḍhāyāḥ svatantro@yaṃ sthitaścidvyomabhairavaḥ ekacinmātrasaṃpūrṇabhairavābhedabhāgini / evamasmītyanāmarśo bhedako bhāvamaṇḍale

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v101] Just as another agent in a dream is not established by any means of knowledge, so everywhere let it be understood that self-awareness alone is self-established.

[tal-a11-v102] Who knows 'I alone am situated' would thus play in the wonderful garden-city of mind, with cities of elements, beings, and truths.

[tal-a11-v103] Thus the thoughts 'I am born' and 'I am dead,' along with all varieties of birth and death, shine as self-created appearances in the wall of mind, within the unborn and immortal.

[tal-a11-v104] In reality, for awareness there is no place or time in either world; awareness is only of other and this world.

[tal-a11-v105] This creation would not have become material if not consciousness-made; that was seen from its middle—by whom, one also earth-bearer?

[tal-a11-v106] At the end of the support-and-supported order of the elements and subtle elements, the power that consists of consciousness, indeed of Śiva's form, is the supporter.

[tal-a11-v107] Therefore perception itself is the doer and sustainer; she is Shiva. From that, states are there as states; power is their supporter; then.

[tal-a11-v108] Even supportless, the imagined does not indeed fall downward; thus the universe, rested in its own support-power, let be considered.

[tal-a11-v109] Of this, the convention 'dense I' and so on is indeed the state of earth and the rest up to the end; 'I am consciousness' is accomplished; Bhairava-self-ness.

[tal-a11-v110] Just as blue and other colors shine in a jewel and a rainbow, so in Shiva, in ultimate reality, these neither arise nor ever decay.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sarvapramāṇairno siddhaṃ svapne kartrantaraṃ yathā / svasaṃvidaḥ svasiddhāyāstathā sarvatra buddhyatām cittacitrapurodyāne krīḍedevaṃ hi vetti yaḥ / ahameva sthito bhūtabhāvatattvapurairiti evaṃ jāto mṛto@smīti janmamṛtyuvicitratāḥ / ajanmanyamṛtau bhānti cittabhittau svanirmitāḥ parehasaṃvidāmātraṃ paralokehalokate / vastutaḥ saṃvido deśaḥ kālo vā naiva kiṃcana abhaviṣyadayaṃ sargo mūrtaścenna tu cinmayaḥ / tadavekṣyata tanmadhyāt kenaiko@pi dharādharaḥ bhūtatanmātravargāderādhārādheyatākrame / ante saṃvinmayī śaktiḥ śivarūpaiva dhāriṇī tasmātpratītirevetthaṃ kartrī dhartrī ca sā śivaḥ / tato bhāvāstatra bhāvāḥ śaktirādhārikā tataḥ sāṃkalpikaṃ nirādhāramapi naiva patatyadhaḥ / svādhāraśaktau viśrāntaṃ viśvamitthaṃ vimṛśyatām asyā ghanāhamityādirūḍhireva dharāditā / yāvadante cidasmīti nirvṛttā bhairavātmatā maṇāvindrāyudhe bhāsa iva nīlādayaḥ śive / paramārthata eṣāṃ tu nodayo na vyayaḥ kvacit

chunks.l2:
[tal-a11-v111] Creation in a place or at a time is inconsistent; indeed, space and time themselves are created by God, who is consciousness itself.

[tal-a11-v112] In waking, opinion is limited to a three-and-a-half-cubit range, a separate watch; in dream, directions and times are varied.

[tal-a11-v113] Therefore we do not regard even a moment as anything at all, since in one action-moment—or in a single moment—many actions occur quickly.

[tal-a11-v114] By that, those who attained the contraction of being at the end of a moment certainly lean on an empty view by this vein.

[tal-a11-v115] Therefore this Lord, our Lord Shiva, lord of freedom and the rest, can make states of being void and make non-being manifest.

[tal-a11-v116] Thus the supreme Lord, of universal form, is praised; but not the fitness of any distinct thing such as earth.

[tal-a11-v117] This has already been stated earlier, so it is not examined again; and through further criticisms of external objects, it is rejected.

[tal-a11-v118] Thus this has been determined: the expansion of sound from kalā and the rest.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-deśe kāle@tra vā sṛṣṭirityetadasamañjasam / cidātmanā hi devena sṛṣṭirdikkālayorapi jāgarābhimate sārdhahastatritayagocare / prahare ca pṛthak svapnāścitradikkālamāninaḥ ata eva kṣaṇaṃ nāma na kiṃcidapi manmahe / kriyākṣaṇe vāpyekasmin bahvyaḥ saṃsyurdrutāḥ kriyāḥ tena ye bhāvasaṃkocaṃ kṣaṇāntaṃ pratipedire / te nūnamenayā nāḍyā śūnyadṛṣṭyavalambinaḥ tadya eṣa sato bhāvāñ śūnyīkartuṃ tathāsataḥ / sphuṭīkartuṃ svatantratvādīśaḥ so@smatprabhuḥ śivaḥ taditthaṃ parameśāno viśvarūpaḥ pragīyate / na tu bhinnasya kasyāpi dharāderupapannatā uktaṃ caitatpuraiveti na bhūyaḥ pravivicyate / bhūyobhiścāpi bāhyārthadūṣaṇaiḥ pravyaramyata taditthameṣa nirṇītaḥ kalādervistaro@dhvanaḥ
